title: Officials and Castles: aki and amely in Descriptions

sections.content: You know *aki* (for people) from A2 Unit 4 and *amely* (for things) from the last lesson. Here they describe the county system: the ispán is a person, so he takes *aki*; the castle is a thing, so it takes *amely*. The table gives the phrases you need for the county system.

sections.title: The county system
rows: a vármegye élén az ispán állt
the ispán stood at the head of the county
a megye székhelye a királyi vár volt
the county seat was the royal castle

items.spanish: IV. Béla, aki a tatárjárás után újjáépítette az országot, arra ösztönözte a nemeseket, hogy kővárakat építsenek.
items.english: Béla IV, who rebuilt the country after the Mongol invasion, urged the nobles to build stone castles.

items.spanish: Az ispán, aki a megye élén állt, a rendért és az adókért felelt.
items.english: The ispán, who stood at the head of the county, was responsible for order and taxes.

items.spanish: A vár, amely a megye székhelye volt, királyi birtok volt.
items.english: The castle, which was the county seat, was a royal estate.

sections.content: Ask first whether the word you describe is a person (*aki*, plural *akik*) or a thing (*amely*, plural *amelyek*). The verb in the relative clause agrees with that word.
